Insomnia & Sleep Disorders

Ailment insomnia sleep nervous-system anxiety stress

Evidence: peer_reviewed

Summary

Sleep disorders characterized by difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or excessive daytime sleepiness, often related to stress and anxiety.

Symptoms

  • difficulty falling asleep
  • frequent awakenings
  • feeling unrested after sleep
  • daytime fatigue
  • irritability
  • concentration problems

  • Valerian Root

Treatment Approaches

  • Historical Traditional sleep aids including valerian root, chamomile tea, and warm milk have been used for centuries across cultures to promote rest.
  • Proven Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), sleep hygiene practices, and short-term use of prescription hypnotics are evidence-based conventional approaches.
  • Experimental CDS Protocol A (chlorine dioxide) before bedtime explored in anecdotal reports; no clinical evidence supports use for sleep disorders.
  • Conventional Sleep scheduling, light exposure management, and treatment of underlying conditions (anxiety, sleep apnea) per clinical guidelines.
